classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught anticlockwise quarter-turn about the origin, locate images in the appropriate quadrants, and recognise that the centre remains fixed.

content.prompt: Mark the given points on a number plane and rotate them $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise about the origin $O$. Write down the coordinates of each image point.

answer.worked: Plot $A$ two units right and one unit down from $O$. Turn $OA$ through $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise, keeping its length unchanged. The image is one unit right and two units up: $A'(1,2)$.
Plot $B$ two units right and one unit up from $O$. Turn $OB$ through $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise, keeping its length unchanged. The image is one unit left and two units up: $B'(-1,2)$.
Plot $C$ three units left and one unit up from $O$. Turn $OC$ through $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise, keeping its length unchanged. The image is one unit left and three units down: $C'(-1,-3)$.
$D$ is the centre of rotation, so it remains fixed: $D'(0,0)$.

spec.description: Complete shared answer graph with labelled original and image points; unit grid spacing is explicit.
